payload.text: A LINE-ORIENTED FILTER CANNOT SEE A PROMPT, AND A PROMPT IS THE EVENT MOST WORTH WAKING SOMEONE FOR. 2026-09-22, my own monitor over the 0.1.6 cut. Its filter carried a [y/N] arm and that arm NEVER FIRED: release: go ahead? [y/N] is printed WITHOUT a trailing newline, so grep --line-buffered had no complete line to flush and held it indefinitely. What actually reached me was the ordinary release: line printed immediately above the prompt -- luck, not design. A cut that printed the prompt with no preamble would have sat blocked in silence, and silence is indistinguishable from still running, which is the couldnt-look-equals-found-nothing collapse arriving through my own instrument for the second time today. Watch the ARTEFACT for a block (the tag ref appearing, a log mtime going stale against date, a process state), never a line filter over a log.
